questions.question: What is the mean proportional between 64 and 4096?
questions.solution:
Given:

First number = 64

Second number = 4096

Concept Used:

Mean proportion = sqrt{atimes b}

Calculation:

⇒ b2 = a times c 

⇒ b2 = 64 times 4096

⇒ b² = 262144

⇒ b = sqrt {262144}=512

**Hence, the mean proportional between 64 and 4096 is 512**

questions.question: When x is added to each of the numbers 7, 11, 18 and 23, then the number so obtained are in proportion. What is the mean proportional between the (x - 1) and (2x - 10)?
questions.solution:
**Calculations:**

The numbers after adding x to 7, 11, 18, and 23 will be: 7 + x, 11 + x, 18 + x, and 23 + x.

Since they are in proportion:

7 + x / 11 + x = 18 + x / 23 + x

Cross multiplying, we get:

(7 + x)(23 + x) = (11 + x)(18 + x)

Expanding both sides:

161 + 30x + x² = 198 + 29x + x²

Canceling x² from both sides:

161 + 30x = 198 + 29x

Simplifying:

30x - 29x = 198 - 161

x = 37

Now, we need to find the mean proportional between x - 1 and 2x - 10.

x - 1 = 37 - 1 = 36

2x - 10 = 2(37) - 10 = 74 - 10 = 64

The mean proportional between 36 and 64 is:

√(36 × 64) = √(2304) = 48

**∴ The mean proportional between x - 1 and 2x - 10 is 48.**

Ram is 20 years older than Rahul. 'n' years ago Ram was thrice as old as Rahul. '2n' years from now the ratio of the ages of Ram and Rahul will be 15 : 11. What is the value of 'n'?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Ram is 20 years older than Rahul.

'n' years ago, Ram was thrice as old as Rahul.

'2n' years from now, the ratio of the ages of Ram and Rahul will be 15:11.

**Formula Used:**

Let's denote the current age of Ram by R and the current age of Rahul by r.

1) R = r + 20

2) R - n = 3(r - n)

3) (R + 2n)/(r + 2n) = (15)/(11)

**Calculation:**

From equation 1:

R = r + 20

From equation 2:

⇒ R - n = 3(r - n)

⇒ r + 20 - n = 3r - 3n

⇒ 2r - 2n = 20

⇒ r - n = 10

From equation 3:

⇒ (R + 2n)/(r + 2n) = (15)/(11)

⇒ 11(R + 2n) = 15(r + 2n)

⇒ 11(r + 20 + 2n) = 15(r + 2n)

⇒ 11r + 220 + 22n = 15r + 30n

⇒ 220 = 4r + 8n

⇒ 55 = r + 2n

We have two equations:

1) r - n = 10

2) r + 2n = 55

Solving these equations:

From r - n = 10:

⇒ r = n + 10

Substitute r in equation r + 2n = 55:

⇒ (n + 10) + 2n = 55

⇒ 3n + 10 = 55

⇒ 3n = 45

⇒ n = 15

**The value of 'n' is 15.**

questions.question: In Class 8 of a school, the ratio of students playing cricket to those playing football is 27 ∶ 13, while the ratio of those playing football to those playing hockey is 26 ∶ 14. If the total number of students in Class 8 is 470, and each student plays exactly one game, find the percentage of students of the class playing cricket. [Give your answer correct to two decimal places.]
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Ratio of students playing cricket to those playing football is 27 : 13 and

Ratio of students playing football to those playing hockey is 26 : 14.

Total no. of students is 470

**Calculations:**

Ratio of students playing cricket, football and hockey respectively is 27 × 26 : 26 × 13 : 13 × 14 

⇒ 702 : 338: 182

⇒ 351: 169 : 91

⇒ 27 : 13 : 7

Now, according to the question, 

(27 + 13 + 7)k = 470

⇒ 47 × k = 470

⇒ k = 10

Now , no. of students playing cricket = 27k = 27 × 10 = 270

Percentage required = 270/470 × 100 = 57.45%** **

**∴ The percentage reduired = 57.45%**

questions.question: Find the third proportional to 27 and 18.
questions.solution:
**Given:-**

Two proportional numbers are 27, 18

**To find:-**

Third proportional number

**Concept used:-**

Proportionality theorem i.e, a : b :: c : d = (a)/(b)=(c)/(d)

**Calculation:-**

Let the third proportional be x

then by proportionality theorem,

27 : 18 :: 18 : x

⇒(27)/(18)=(18)/(x)

⇒x=(18×18)/(27)

⇒x = 12

**The value of the third proportional is 12.**

questions.question: 65% of Samita's income is equal to 91% of Bhairav's income. If Samita's income was Rs. 1,500 more than what it is and Bhairav's income was Rs. 500 more than what it is, the ratio of the incomes of Samita and Bhairav would have been 3 ∶ 2. What is the actual combined income (in Rs. ) of Samita and Bhairav?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

65 % of Samita's income = 91 % of Bhairav's income

Samita's new income is 1500 more than her current income 

Bhairav's new income is 500 more than her current income

The new ratio of Samita and Bhairav's income = 3 : 2

**Calculation:**

Let Samita's current income = p Rs. and Bhairav's current income = q Rs.

According to the question,

65 % of p = 91 % of q

⇒ 65 × p = 91× q

⇒ p/q = 91/65 = 7/5

Let's assume that ,

⇒Samita's current income (p) = 7k

⇒Bhairav's current income (q) = 5k

Samita's new income = 1500 + Samita' s current income

⇒Samita's new income = 1500 + 7k

Bhairav's new income = 500 + Bhairav's current income

⇒Bhairav's new income = 500 + 5k

The new ratio of incomes of Samita and Bhairav = 3:2

⇒(1500 + 7k)/(500 + 5k) = 3/2

⇒3000 + 14k = 1500 + 15k

⇒ k = 1500

The income of Samita = 7k = 7 x 1500 = 10500 Rs.

The income of Bhairav = 5k = 5 x 1500 = 7500 Rs.

The combined incomes of Samita and Bhairav = 10500 + 7500 = 18000 Rs.

**∴ The Actual combined income of Samita and Bhairav is 18000 Rs.**

questions.question: If P : Q = 10 : 11 and Q : R = 11 : 12, then P + Q : Q + R : R + P is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

P : Q = 10 : 11 and Q : R = 11 : 12

**Concept used:**

Combining ratios

**Calculation:**

P : Q = 10 : 11 ----(i)

Q : R = 11 : 12 ----(ii)

Since in both the ratios (i) and (ii) the combining one,Q, has the same value in both the cases 

Hence, P : Q : R = 10 : 11 : 12

Let P , Q , and R be 10x ,11x , and 12x respectively, where x is the factor by which ratio is changing-

then, P + Q = 10x + 11x = 21x

Q + R = 11x +12x = 23x

P + R = 10x + 12x = 22x

⇒ P + Q : Q + R : R + P = 21x : 23x : 22x

⇒P + Q : Q + R : R + P = 21 : 23 : 22 (by putting x = 1)

**∴ The value of P + Q : Q + R : R + P is 21 : 23 : 22**

Given that x varies directly as y and x = 45 when y = 9. What is the value of x when y = 50?
questions.solution:
Concept:

When two quantities are directly proportional to each other, then their ratio is constant.

x ∝ y

⇒ x / y = k

where k is the constant of proportionality.

Calculation:

As per the given data,

⇒ (45)/( 9) = k

⇒ k = 5

So, (x)/(y) = 5 ---(1)

Putting y = 50 in equation (1),

⇒ (x)/(50) = 5

⇒ x = 250

∴ The value of x when y is 50 is 250.

questions.question: What is the ratio of the mean proportional between 1.2 and 10.8 to the third proportional to 0.2 and 1.2?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

First and third proportional = 1.2 and 10.8

First and second proportional = 0.2 and 1.2

**Concept used:**

If a, b and c are in proportion then:

Mean proportional:

⇒ b² = a × c

Third proportional:

⇒ c = b²/a

**Calculation:**

Let mean proportional be x and third proportional be y.

⇒ x² = 1.2 × 10.8

⇒ x = 3.6

Again, 

⇒ y = (1.2)²/0.2 = 7.2

Now, ratio of x to y = 3.6 : 7.2 = 1 : 2

**∴ Ratio of mean proportional to the third proportional will be 1 : 2 **

questions.question: P got married 15 years ago. Today her age is 1(3)/(5) times her age at the time of her marriage. At present her son's age is (1)/(5) of her age. What was her son's age 4 years ago as a fraction of P's age at that time?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of P's present age to age at marriage = 1(3/5) = 8 : 5.

Difference of 3 parts = 15 years ⇒ 1 part = 5 years.

P's present age = 8 × 5 = 40 years.

Son's present age = 40 × (1/5) = 8 years.

4 years ago, Son = 4 years and P = 36 years. Required fraction = 4 / 36 = 1/9.

**∴ The correct answer is 1/9.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

P's present age = 1(3/5) × (P's age 15 years ago) = 8/5 × (P's age 15 years ago)

Son's present age = 1/5 × (P's present age)

 Age Timeline
 
 
 Present Age
 P = 40 yrs
 Son = 8 yrs

 
 4 Years Ago
 P = 36 yrs
 Son = 4 yrs

 
 
 

 
 
 
• 
 − 4 years
 
 
 Ratio = 4 / 36 = 1 / 9

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let P's present age be x.

⇒ Age of P 15 years ago = x − 15

⇒ x = (8/5) × (x − 15)

⇒ 5x = 8x − 120

⇒ 3x = 120

⇒ x = 40 years

⇒ P's present age = 40 years.

⇒ Present age of son = (1/5) × 40 = 8 years.

⇒ 4 years ago, P's age = 40 − 4 = 36 years.

⇒ 4 years ago, Son's age = 8 − 4 = 4 years.

⇒ Required fraction = 4 / 36 = 1 / 9.

**∴ The correct answer is 1/9.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Ratio of Ages

If the ratio of ages of two persons is a:b, their ages can be represented as ax and bx. The age difference between two persons always remains constant over time.

Fractional Relationships

A relationship given as 1(3/5) times means a multiplying factor of 8/5. Expressing conditions as fractions directly yields a simple linear equation.

Problems on Ages

It is highly recommended to always calculate the present ages first. This establishes a fixed reference point before finding any past or future ages.
